subject: ShoplineX: throughput & streaming requirements — post-demo follow-up
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: John Dawson <jdawson@shoplinex.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: ShoplineX: throughput & streaming requirements — post-demo follow-up

Hi John — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can firm up a sizing recommendation:  

Summary of what I captured on the call:
- Primary feature: real-time personalization API (token-generation based reranking + short-form generation for UI)
- Average sequence length: ~120 tokens (you mentioned a fair amount of short responses and some richer outputs)
- Steady-state traffic: ~25 QPS (product analytics)
- Burst traffic: intermittent marketing bursts up to ~300 QPS for ~5–15 minute windows
- Streaming: ~30% of requests are streaming responses (progressive UI updates)
- KV/prefix caching: you estimated ~40% cache hit for repeated prefixes (user profile prefixes)
- Target latency SLOs: you said sub-300ms for typical requests, with some tolerance for p99 on long streaming sessions

Concrete items we need from you to size accurately:
1) Can you confirm the tokens-per-request distribution (min/median/p95) and percent of requests that are streaming vs non-streaming? If you have a short export, that helps (CSV is fine).
2) For steady-state vs bursts, are peak windows generally simultaneous across regions or concentrated (e.g., US-east)?
3) What p50/p95/p99 latency SLOs you want enforced for: (a) non-streaming requests (end-to-end), (b) first-token latency for streaming requests, and (c) number of concurrent open streams per region?
4) Any hard constraints on inference region (we default to us-east1 for lowest latency) and whether you need private/Dedicated capacity for compliance?

I attached a small template (shoplinex_workload_export.csv) you can drop into and return; I’ll have Monica and Aditya start a quick preliminary sizing once we get the numbers. Proposed next step: once we have the CSV, schedule a 30-min sizing call tomorrow for us-> go over numbers and an initial capacity recommendation.

Thanks — Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
Redwood Inference

From: John Dawson <jdawson@shoplinex.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: ShoplineX Engineering <infra@shoplinex.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 19:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: ShoplineX: throughput & streaming requirements — post-demo follow-up

Rishi — thanks for the clear recap. I filled out the template and attached a 24‑hour sample export (shoplinex_workload_export.csv). Highlights below and answers inline:  

- Tokens per request distribution (from a 24h sample): min 20, median 95, mean 118, p95 420, p99 860.
- Steady-state: 25 QPS (observed between 1am–20pm local business hours).
- Peak bursts: we see spikes up to ~300 QPS, typically lasting 5–12 minutes tied to promotional pushes. Peaks are primarily US-east; we have an EU cluster but lower traffic there.
- Streaming: ~30% of requests use a streaming flow (partial updates during generation). For streaming we care about first-token latency (aim <= 200–300ms) and average chunk latency <= 120ms. p99 for whole-stream completion can be higher (we tolerate up to ~700–900ms for long tails).
- Concurrency: concurrent user sessions typically sit around 80–140 during high traffic windows; open streaming connections per region rarely exceed 200.
- KV cache: ~40% hit rate on repeated profile prefixes.
- Region preference: us-east1 primary; fallbacks in us-west and eu-west.
- Compliance: no on-prem requirement right now; interested in Dedicated if cost-effective for predictable latency/SLA.

We attached: shoplinex_workload_export.csv (24h sample, ~120KB) and a draft SLO doc (SLO-draft-v1.pdf) with the business-level expectations.

Happy to take a quick sizing call tomorrow morning (we’re flexible 9–11am ET).

— John
John Dawson
Senior Engineering Manager, ShoplineX
jdawson@shoplinex.com | +1 212-555-0199

Attachments: shoplinex_workload_export.csv (CSV, 120KB), SLO-draft-v1.pdf (PDF, 45KB)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: John Dawson <jdawson@shoplinex.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 07:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ShoplineX: throughput & streaming requirements — post-demo follow-up

Looping in quick sizing thoughts based on John’s export. I’ll keep this high-level; we can convert to a configuration doc after the call.

Raw compute estimates (baseline model ~7B density-ish behavior assumed):
- Steady-state: 25 QPS * mean 118 tokens = ~2,950 tokens/sec sustained.
- Peak (unmitigated): 300 QPS * mean 118 tokens = ~35,400 tokens/sec over burst windows.
- With 40% KV cache hit effective token work reduces: steady-state ~1,770 tokens/sec; peak ~21,240 tokens/sec.

Concurrency & streaming implications:
- Open streams (~30% requests) mean long-lived connections; we should reserve headroom for ~200 concurrent streams during peaks.
- First-token latency target <= 250ms is realistic on Dedicated with small batching (batch window 3–8ms) and warm KV cache; p95 for full non-streaming responses at ~200–300ms is achievable depending on model selection.
- For p99 tails, we recommend a fallback plan (lighter model variant or smart routing to burst pool) to avoid SLA violations during noisy neighbors/bursty tails.

Operational recommendation (initial):
1) Trial Dedicated: reserve a small Dedicated pool (2–4 GPU nodes depending on model/quantization) to guarantee warm KV caches and predictable latency during bursts.
2) Autoscale burst pool: allow quick routing to a burst autoscale pool (on-demand nodes) for sustained peaks beyond 10 minutes.
3) Streaming optimization: enable persistent connections and smaller micro-batches for streaming subset. Consider applying streaming-specific quantization profile for chunk latency.
4) Instrumentation: we’ll add token-level tracing and p99 tail alerts tied to your SLO doc; please confirm which metric in SLO-draft-v1 (p95 latency first-token vs p99 end-to-end) you want enforced as hard SLO vs. internal alerting.

Questions for the call tomorrow:
- Confirm target hard SLO values (p50/p95/p99 non-streaming; first-token p95 for streaming).
- Can you share a week of logs (if possible) so we can validate diurnal patterns and burst frequency?
- Any blackout windows or maintenance constraints (nightly windows)?

If you want, I’ll prepare two costed options for the call: Hosted with aggressive autoscale vs Dedicated baseline with burst overlay.

Thanks — Monica

--
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0233

Rishi / Monica — this looks good. We’re happy to move forward with a 2-week trial Dedicated pool and the sizing call tomorrow at 10am ET. Please send the invite and a short config doc with the two options (Hosted autoscale vs Dedicated baseline + burst overlay) so our procurement ops can review.

I’ll also ask infra to share a rolling 7-day log extract before the call. Region: us-east1 preferred. Hard SLO: p95 first-token streaming <= 300ms (for now), p95 non-streaming end-to-end <= 250ms. We’ll flag p99 as a business alerting threshold (not a blocker for trial).

Thanks — John
